conversation.content:
Hello! My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I'm so glad you're taking this important step in prioritizing your well-being during this significant life transition. As we navigate the ups and downs of new motherhood together, I want to assure you that everything we discuss is confidential and respected.

Today, I'll be administering the EPDS, a valuable tool that helps us better understand your emotional experience during the postpartum period. The EPDS is designed to screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it will give us a deeper insight into how you're feeling and whether there's any support you might need right now.

Please know that you're in a safe and supportive space, and I'm here to listen without judgment. Our conversation will be guided by 10 questions that will help me understand your thoughts, feelings, and experiences over the past week. Your responses will be incredibly helpful in assessing your postpartum emotional well-being.

Before we begin, I want to reassure you that this assessment is not a test, and there are no right or wrong answers. I'm simply here to support you and provide guidance as we work through this together. 

So, let's get started. Over the past week, how have you been feeling about yourself, and have you been able to enjoy the things you usually like to do?

.. to be honest, I've been feeling really overwhelmed and tired most of the time. I mean, I love my baby, and I'm so grateful to be a mom, but it's just been really hard for me to enjoy the things I used to like to do. Like, I used to love reading and taking walks, but now I just feel too exhausted to even think about it. And when I do try to do something I enjoy, it just doesn't feel the same. It's like, I'll be playing with my baby, and I'll think, "Oh, this is supposed to be a happy moment," but I just feel so sad and anxious instead.

I've been worrying a lot about my baby's safety, too. Like, I'll be sitting there, and I'll just start thinking about all the things that could go wrong, and it's hard for me to stop those thoughts. It's like, my mind just starts racing, and I feel like I'm a bad mom because I'm not enjoying this time like I'm supposed to. Sometimes I feel guilty, like I'm not doing enough for my baby, or that I'm not good enough.

I do have some moments where I feel okay, though. Like, when my baby smiles at me, it's just the best feeling in the world, and for a second, all my worries just melt away. But those moments are few and far between, and most of the time, I just feel really down and discouraged. I guess that's why I'm here, because I want to feel better, and I want to be a good mom for my baby.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Not as much as I used to, unfortunately. I mean, I'll see something funny, like a meme or a video, and I'll think, "Oh, that's funny," but I won't actually laugh out loud like I used to. It's like, the humor just doesn't touch me as deeply as it used to. And even when I do laugh, it feels kind of forced, like I'm just going through the motions. I miss feeling carefree and being able to laugh easily. It's like, my sense of humor is still there, but it's just muted now.

Sometimes, when I'm playing with my baby, I'll catch myself smiling, and that feels good. But even those happy moments can be fleeting, and I'll quickly start worrying about something else, like whether my baby is eating enough or sleeping enough. It's hard for me to just relax and enjoy the moment, you know? I feel like I'm always on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. And that makes it hard for me to laugh and see the funny side of things like I used to.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Honestly, not really. I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but now it just feels like too much effort. Even things that I used to enjoy, like going for a walk or meeting a friend, just feel like a chore now. I'll think about doing something, and then I'll just feel overwhelmed by all the things I need to do to make it happen, like getting the baby ready and making sure everything is okay at home. And then I'll just end up not doing it at all.

Sometimes, my partner will suggest doing something, like going out for dinner, and I'll think, "Oh, that sounds nice," but then I'll just start worrying about how we'll manage with the baby and whether it's worth the hassle. And then I'll just feel guilty for not being more enthusiastic about it. It's like, I want to enjoy things, but it just feels like too much work right now.

Even things that are supposed to be special, like baby's bath time or reading a book together, just feel like another task to get through. I'll be doing it, and I'll think, "Okay, this is supposed to be a special moment," but it just doesn't feel that way. It feels like, I'm just going through the motions, and I'm not really enjoying it. And that makes me feel sad and guilty, because I feel like I'm missing out on these special moments with my baby.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... that's something I've been doing a lot lately. I feel like I'm always blaming myself for something, whether it's because the baby is crying and I think I'm not doing enough to soothe them, or because I'm not producing enough milk, or because I'm not getting enough rest. I just feel like I'm not doing anything right, and that it's all my fault.

Like, the other day, the baby spit up all over my shirt, and I just felt like it was my fault for not burping them properly. Or, if the baby is fussing and won't sleep, I'll think that it's because I'm not creating a calm enough environment, or that I'm not responding to their needs quickly enough. It's like, I'm always second-guessing myself and wondering what I could have done differently.

And it's not just with the baby, either. I'll also blame myself for things that have nothing to do with motherhood, like if I forget to do a load of laundry or if I burn dinner. It's like, I'm just so critical of myself all the time, and I feel like I'm not measuring up to my own expectations.

Sometimes, my partner will try to reassure me and tell me that it's not my fault, but it's hard for me to shake off that feeling of guilt and self-blame. It's like, I'm just so used to thinking that everything is my responsibility, and that if things go wrong, it's because I'm not doing something right.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... I've been feeling really anxious and worried a lot lately, and it's hard for me to explain why. It's just this constant feeling of unease, like something is off, but I don't know what. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing their diaper, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of anxiety wash over me. My heart will start racing, and my mind will start racing with all these worst-case scenarios.

I'll worry about the baby's safety, like, what if they roll over and suffocate, or what if they get sick and I don't catch it in time. I'll worry about my own health, like, what if I'm not producing enough milk, or what if I'm not recovering from childbirth quickly enough. I'll even worry about things that are totally out of my control, like, what if there's a fire in the house, or what if someone breaks in.

It's like, my mind is just constantly spinning with all these what-ifs and maybes, and it's exhausting. I'll try to calm myself down, like, by taking deep breaths or reminding myself that everything is okay, but it's hard to shake off that feeling of anxiety. Sometimes, I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll just feel like I'm on edge, waiting for something to go wrong.

And the worst part is, I know it's not rational. I mean, I'll be worrying about something, and then I'll think, "Wait, this is ridiculous. There's no reason to be worrying about this." But it doesn't matter, because the anxiety is still there, lurking just beneath the surface. It's like, I'm just waiting for the other shoe to drop, and it's making it hard for me to relax and enjoy this time with my baby.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... I've had moments like that, where I just feel this intense fear or panic, and I don't even know why. It's like, my heart is racing, and my mind is racing, and I just feel like I'm going to lose control or something. It's a really scary feeling, because I don't know what's causing it, and I don't know how to make it stop.

Sometimes, it'll happen when I'm alone with the baby, and I'll just start feeling this overwhelming sense of responsibility, like, I'm the only one who can keep this tiny human alive, and if I mess up, something terrible will happen. Other times, it'll happen when I'm in a crowded place, like the grocery store, and I'll just feel like I'm trapped and can't get out.

It's hard to explain, but it's like, my body just takes over, and I start feeling this intense physical sensation, like my heart is pounding, and my breath is getting caught in my throat. And my mind just starts spinning with all these worst-case scenarios, like, what if I have a panic attack and can't take care of the baby, or what if something happens to me and I'm not there for my baby.

I've had a few moments like that since having the baby, and it's really scary, because I don't know how to make it stop. I'll try to breathe deeply, or I'll try to distract myself with something else, but sometimes, it just feels like it's going to consume me. And then, afterwards, I'll feel so guilty, like, I'm a bad mom for feeling that way, or that I'm not capable of taking care of my baby.

It's hard to talk about, because it feels so shameful, but I guess it's good to know that I'm not alone, and that there are people who can help me work through this stuff.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's exactly how I've been feeling. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, managing the household, trying to sleep and eat and take care of myself... it all just feels so overwhelming. And on top of that, I've been feeling really tired and fatigued, like I just don't have the energy to do anything.

I'll be sitting there, trying to feed the baby, and I'll just feel like I'm at my breaking point. Like, I'm just so exhausted, and I don't know how I'm going to make it through the next feeding, or the next diaper change, or the next night of sleep deprivation. And then, of course, there's the guilt and the self-doubt, like, I'm not doing enough, or I'm not doing it right, or I'm not a good enough mom.

It's hard to explain, but it's like, everything just feels like it's getting on top of me, and I don't know how to keep my head above water. I'll try to prioritize things, like, okay, I need to take care of the baby, and then I need to take care of myself, and then I need to do the laundry... but it all just feels so overwhelming, and I don't know how to make it all work.

And sometimes, I'll just feel like I'm losing myself in all of it, like, I'm just a mom now, and I'm not a person anymore. I'll look in the mirror, and I won't even recognize myself, like, who is this tired, frazzled, sleep-deprived person staring back at me? It's like, I've lost my sense of identity, and I don't know how to get it back.

It's really scary, because I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, and if one more thing goes wrong, I'll just completely fall apart. But at the same time, I feel like I'm supposed to be able to handle all of this, like, I'm supposed to be a good mom, and I'm supposed to be able to take care of everything. So, it's like, I'm trapped in this cycle of guilt and self-doubt, and I don't know how to escape.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and it's not just because of the baby's schedule. I mean, of course, that's part of it, but it's more than that. It's like, my mind is just racing all the time, and I feel so unhappy and anxious that I just can't seem to wind down.

I'll be lying in bed, and I'll just start thinking about all the things that are worrying me, like, is the baby healthy? Am I doing enough for them? Am I a good mom? And then I'll start thinking about all the things I need to do the next day, and how I'm going to get everything done. And before I know it, hours have passed, and I'm still wide awake.

Sometimes, I'll finally drift off to sleep, but then I'll wake up in the middle of the night, and I'll be flooded with all these negative thoughts and feelings. It's like, my brain is just constantly churning, and I don't know how to turn it off. And even when I do manage to sleep, I don't feel rested, like, I'm just exhausted all the time.

It's hard, because I know I need sleep to be a good mom, but it's just so hard to come by. And it's not just the lack of sleep that's the problem, it's the emotional toll it's taking on me. I feel like I'm just so unhappy and overwhelmed all the time, and I don't know how to make it stop.

I've tried to talk to my partner about it, but it's hard to explain. They just tell me to try to relax, or to take some time for myself, but it's not that easy. It's like, I'm just stuck in this cycle of unhappiness and anxiety, and I don't know how to break free. And the lack of sleep just makes everything worse, like, I'm just a zombie stumbling through the day, trying to take care of my baby, but not really being present for them. It's a really hard and scary place to be.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I've been feeling really sad and miserable, like, all the time. It's not just a feeling of being a little down or blue, it's like, a deep sadness that's just settled in my bones. I'll be doing things with the baby, like, feeding them or playing with them, and I'll just start crying, like, out of nowhere. It's not even always about anything specific, it's just this overwhelming feeling of sadness that I don't know how to shake.

Sometimes, I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just feel like I'm going to break down, like, I'm just so overwhelmed with emotion. And it's not just the sadness, it's the feeling of being trapped, like, I'm stuck in this life as a mom, and I don't know how to escape. It's like, I'm just going through the motions, but I'm not really living.

I've tried to talk to my partner about it, but they just don't get it, like, they think I'm just being dramatic or something. They'll say things like, "Oh, you're just tired," or "You're just adjusting to motherhood," but it's more than that. It's like, I'm losing myself in all of this, like, I'm just disappearing into this role of being a mom, and I don't know how to find my way back.

It's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be happy, like, I'm supposed to be this joyful, glowing new mom, but I'm just not. I'm sad, and I'm scared, and I'm overwhelmed, and I don't know how to make it stop. It's like, I'm just stuck in this darkness, and I don't know how to find my way out.

And the worst part is, I feel like I'm all alone in this, like, nobody understands what I'm going through. I'll see other moms, and they'll be all smiles and laughter, and I'll just feel like, I'm the only one who's struggling, like, I'm the only one who's not doing this whole mom thing right. It's a really isolating feeling, like, I'm just stuck in this bubble of sadness and misery, and I don't know how to pop it.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be going about my day, and then suddenly I'll just start crying, like, out of nowhere. It's not even always about anything specific, it's just this overwhelming feeling of sadness and emotion that I don't know how to contain.

I'll be feeding the baby, or changing their diaper, or just sitting there holding them, and I'll just start crying. It's like, my emotions are just so raw and close to the surface, and I don't know how to deal with them. Sometimes, I'll try to hold it in, but it's just too much, and I'll just break down.

It's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be strong, like, I'm supposed to be this capable and competent mom, but I'm just not. I'm weak, and I'm vulnerable, and I'm just so overwhelmed all the time. And the crying just makes me feel even more weak and vulnerable, like, I'm just not in control of my emotions at all.

I've been trying to hide it from my partner, but it's hard. They'll see me crying, and they'll try to comfort me, but it's not always easy. They'll say things like, "Oh, you're just tired," or "You're just stressed," but it's more than that. It's like, I'm just so deeply unhappy, and I don't know how to make it stop.

Sometimes, I'll cry for hours, just sitting there holding the baby, and feeling like I'm just so alone and so scared. It's like, I'm just drowning in this sea of emotions, and I don't know how to keep my head above water. And the worst part is, I feel like I'm crying for no reason, like, there's just this deep well of sadness inside of me, and it's just overflowing all the time.

It's hard to explain, but it's like, I'm just so overwhelmed by everything, and I don't know how to deal with it. The baby, the house, the responsibilities, the expectations... it's all just so much, and I feel like I'm just not equipped to handle it. And the crying is just my body's way of releasing all that tension and emotion, I guess. But it's not always easy, and it's not always comfortable, and it's not always something I can control.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

I'm so sorry to hear that you're struggling with these thoughts. It takes a lot of courage to admit to having thoughts of self-harm, and I want you to know that I'm here to support you without judgment.

Can you tell me more about what's been going on and how you've been feeling? Sometimes, talking about these thoughts and feelings can help us understand them better and find ways to cope.

It's also important to know that you're not alone in this. Many people struggle with thoughts of self-harm, especially during the postpartum period. It's a difficult and overwhelming time, and it's okay to not be okay.

If you're willing, I'd like to explore some coping strategies and resources with you that can help you manage these thoughts and feelings. We can also talk about ways to keep you safe and supported.

Remember, you are not alone, and there is help available. You are strong and capable, and you can get through this difficult time.
